subject: Penetration test report request & secure transfer playbook
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@orchidhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: latest penetration test report (hosted API) + transfer options

Hi Laura,

Hope you’re well. We’re doing a quarterly security intake for Orchid Health and need the most recent penetration test report covering Redwood’s hosted API (production). Can you confirm:

- Do you have the latest PT report that includes the hosted API endpoints and authentication flows?
- What parts of your environment were in-scope (prod only, staging, infra)?
- How do you prefer to share the report securely? Our portal does not accept presigned S3 links, and procurement requires encrypted delivery with evidence of redaction.

Can we get the report by COB 2027-04-23? If the full report can’t be shared, a redacted reviewer copy + a statement of scope would work. Also, please indicate whether your team can sign an NDA or execute an ATO checklist for reviewers.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround.

Best,
Alice
Security Program Manager
Orchid Health
alice.park@orchidhealth.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest penetration test report (hosted API) + transfer options

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the note. We can provide a redacted reviewer copy of the most recent penetration test (completed 2027-03) that covers the hosted API production endpoints and auth flows. High-level scope: external network testing against public API endpoints, auth flows (API keys + OAuth redirect flows), and application-layer vuln validation. Internal infra (private orchestration, hypervisor layer) was explicitly excluded in this engagement. I’ll include a short scope statement with the report.

Secure transfer options we support (pick one):

1) SFTP to a customer-provided endpoint (SFTP server + user). We can push a time-limited account, and rotate the account after download.

2) Short-lived reviewer account in Redwood Secure Reviewer Portal (web UI) — access expires after 7 days, IP allowlist and MFA available.

3) Encrypted ZIP (AES-256) delivered via our file transfer service; password will be shared via a separate channel (phone/secure chat).

4) Pre-signed, IP-restricted S3 URL with 48-hour expiry (only if your portal can ingest presigned objects).

Our standard redaction process removes customer-facing PII and internal-only service identifiers; final redaction is reviewed by Security & Legal. Typical turnaround for redaction + packaging is ~36–48 hours from approval.

I’ve attached a short transfer playbook outlining the above methods and our checklist (transfer-playbook-v1.0.txt). If Orchid requires an executed NDA for reviewers, we can sign — let me know the contact and a copy.

Which transfer method do you prefer? If SFTP is best, please reply with hostname, preferred username, and any IP allowlist that we should use.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Compliance (on rotation)
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest penetration test report (hosted API) + transfer options

Looping in Irene for the redaction work and to confirm secure transfer mechanics. Heads-up on recommended approach from SecOps:

- If the customer portal won't accept presigned links, SFTP push to a customer-provided endpoint is simplest and auditable. We should request a one-time account and an IP allowlist.
- If they prefer a hosted reviewer account, we can create it with expiring access and enable MFA; we'll capture access logs for the record.
- For extra assurance, we can provide a SHA256 checksum of the delivered file and include a redaction manifest (which fields were removed).

Irene — can you confirm ETA for redaction and whether any technical findings require additional vendor coordination before redaction?

Ben
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest penetration test report (hosted API) + transfer options

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the quick reply and context. Per your note that the Orchid portal won’t ingest presigned S3 objects, we’ll proceed with an SFTP push. Planned steps:

1) Security will perform final redaction (we removed internal-only hostnames and staff emails). Redaction completed — attached: redacted_PT_2027-03.pdf (redacted reviewer copy).

2) We’ll push the file to your SFTP endpoint once you confirm hostname + user. After transfer we’ll rotate/delete the account and provide a delivery audit (username, timestamp, SHA256).

SFTP details we need from Orchid: hostname, preferred username, allowed source IPs (we’ll provide ours), and whether passive/active mode is required. If you’d rather receive the file via our Secure Reviewer Portal, we can set up an expiring reviewer account instead (7-day access, IP allowlist, MFA).

If you need a signed evidence letter or an NDA executed prior to delivery, please attach the form and we’ll route to Legal.

Attachments:
- redacted_PT_2027-03.pdf (redacted reviewer copy, PDF)
- transfer-playbook-v1.0.txt (transfer checklist and instructions)

Let me know which transfer option you prefer and the SFTP details if applicable. If you prefer a phone call to share the encryption password, I’m available tomorrow between 9–11am PT.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Compliance
Redwood Inference
